name: OpenSearch
model: JSON documents in indexes, full-text search, aggregations, k-NN vector search; query DSL, SQL and PPL
engine_note: Apache Lucene segments (immutable, merged), inverted indexes; k-NN plugin uses Lucene HNSW or Faiss (HNSW, IVF); translog for durability
consistency: Single-document atomic; no multi-document transactions. Translog fsync before ack by default (index.translog.durability=request). Near real-time: docs searchable after refresh (default 1 s). Replica reads can lag the primary.
scaling: Horizontal: primary shards plus replicas spread across nodes; optional remote-backed storage and segment replication put segments in object storage; Amazon OpenSearch Serverless separates compute and storage.

licence_events.event: AWS announces a fork of Apache-licensed Elasticsearch 7.10.2 and Kibana after Elastic's SSPL/ELv2 change; released as OpenSearch (Apache 2.0)
AWS moves OpenSearch to the new OpenSearch Software Foundation under the Linux Foundation (governance change; licence stays Apache 2.0)

reach: Reach for it when you want Elasticsearch-style search and log analytics under a plain Apache 2.0 licence, or you are on AWS and want the managed service there.
avoid: Avoid as the system of record or when you need transactions across documents; avoid if you rely on Elastic-only features added after the 2021 fork.
escape: Same reason as Elasticsearch: ranked text search and log analytics beyond Postgres full-text search, Apache licensed.
chat: A hybrid keyword plus vector index over message text, fed from the messages table.
notes: LF press release 2024-09-16 quote (AWS): 'By transferring OpenSearch to the Linux Foundation, we are setting the project and its community up for its next stage of growth.' No Jepsen analysis found in the jepsen.io index. Translog default and refresh behaviour inherited from the Elasticsearch 7.10 fork; the OpenSearch index-settings page lists index.translog.durability default request (not re-fetched verbatim: unconfirmed wording). AWS fork post (2021-01-21) quote: 'AWS will step up to create and maintain a ALv2-licensed fork of open source Elasticsearch and Kibana.'
